fitReason: Strong intersection of statistical learning, robotic policy representations and foundation-model rewards. His recent co-advised USC work offers a concrete methods-to-hardware connection for a CS-oriented research visit, particularly action-label efficiency and reliable policy improvement.

physicalEvidence.summary: CLAM’s full July 30, 2026 revision and all-USC author project verify actual WidowX manipulation across four tasks at 5 Hz, using continuous latent actions grounded by limited action-labeled play data. Table III uses ten trials per task with half-credit for partial completion, rather than pure binary success. Tu is explicitly an equal adviser. Separately, the May 2026 Robometer revision deploys learned rewards for policy improvement on real Franka Panda, SO-101 and bimanual platforms; its online loop still needs human physical resets. This is learned execution, distinct from recorded-trajectory reward evaluation and simulation.
